executive_summary: ECN-042 adds an adjustable early load warning, hysteresis, overload-event logging, CAN event reporting, and fail-safe behavior for invalid load or boom-angle inputs. The primary changes are expected in firmware, HMI/configuration, storage handling, CAN communications, and verification. Hardware changes to the existing sensors and lift-inhibit relay are explicitly excluded.
detected_change: Extend the existing Safe Load Indicator controller with configurable pre-warning, overload data logging/communication, and sensor-invalid fail-safe behavior while preserving unaffected legacy warning/inhibit functions.

requirements.requirement: The pre-warning threshold shall be configurable from 80% to 90% of SWL.
requirements.evidence: Requested change A specifies an allowed setting of 80% to 90% of SWL.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: A user-configurable threshold accepts values within 80–90% SWL and rejects or prevents values outside that range.
requirements.ambiguity: The configuration interface, step size, permissions, and persistence behavior are not stated.

requirements.requirement: The default pre-warning threshold shall be 85% of SWL.
requirements.evidence: Requested change A states 85% as the default.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: A controller using default settings has a pre-warning threshold of 85% SWL.
requirements.ambiguity: It is not stated whether firmware upgrade should reset existing units to this default.

requirements.requirement: After pre-warning activates, it shall remain active until calculated load is at least 5 percentage points below the configured threshold.
requirements.evidence: Requested change B defines a 5 percentage-point release hysteresis.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: For threshold T, warning remains active above T-5 percentage points and clears only when calculated load reaches or falls below the intended release boundary, subject to clarification of exact boundary semantics.
requirements.ambiguity: The exact inclusive/exclusive comparison at T-5 is not formally stated.

requirements.requirement: Every event at or above 100% SWL shall be logged.
requirements.evidence: Requested change C requires logging every event in which calculated load reaches or exceeds 100% SWL.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: An overload event at the defined detection point creates one retained event record; event start/end de-duplication behavior requires clarification.
requirements.ambiguity: The definition of a distinct event is not stated, so repeated samples during one continuous overload could create duplicate records.

requirements.requirement: Each overload record shall include timestamp, calculated load, boom angle, and operating radius.
requirements.evidence: Requested change C lists four required record fields.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Every stored overload record contains all four fields and each value corresponds to the detected event.
requirements.ambiguity: Timestamp source/resolution and numeric encoding/resolution are not specified.

requirements.requirement: Internal storage shall retain at least 10,000 overload-event records.
requirements.evidence: Requested change D states at least 10,000 records.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The device can store and subsequently access at least 10,000 valid overload records without loss caused by nominal operation.
requirements.ambiguity: Behavior when storage becomes full is explicitly open.

requirements.requirement: The latest overload event shall be transmitted over the existing CAN interface using identifier 0x18FF50E5 within 500 ms of detection.
requirements.evidence: Requested change E states the CAN identifier and 500 ms timing.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: For a detected overload event, a message using CAN ID 0x18FF50E5 is initiated within 500 ms and represents that event.
requirements.ambiguity: CAN payload mapping, byte order, scaling, retry behavior, and what constitutes transmission completion are not specified.

requirements.requirement: If load input or boom-angle input remains invalid continuously for more than 200 ms, the controller shall show sensor fault and activate the existing lift-inhibit relay.
requirements.evidence: Requested change F defines invalid-input duration and two required responses.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: A continuously invalid load or angle input crossing the specified duration causes both sensor-fault indication and lift-inhibit activation; recovery behavior requires clarification.
requirements.ambiguity: Invalidity criteria, exact timing boundary, latching/recovery behavior, and distinction between which sensor failed are not specified.

requirements.requirement: The load sensor, angle sensor, and lift-inhibit relay hardware shall not be changed by this ECN.
requirements.evidence: Requested change G explicitly excludes changes to those hardware items.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: The released implementation uses the existing load sensor, angle sensor, and lift-inhibit relay hardware.
requirements.ambiguity: Other controller hardware changes are not explicitly prohibited.

requirements.requirement: Existing warning and inhibit behavior not modified by ECN-042 shall continue to work.
requirements.evidence: Requested change H requires preservation of unaffected existing behavior.
requirements.acceptance_criteria: Regression testing shows existing warning and inhibit functions outside the stated ECN modifications still behave as in the approved baseline.
requirements.ambiguity: The authoritative baseline specification and regression set are not provided.

impacts.impact: Add configurable threshold and release hysteresis without changing the existing 100% inhibit function.
impacts.rationale: REQ-001 to REQ-003 change warning state behavior.

impacts.impact: Add continuous invalid-input timing and fail-safe output behavior.
impacts.rationale: REQ-008 requires time-qualified invalidity detection and two outputs.

impacts.impact: Create overload event records, capacity handling, data integrity behavior, and retrieval/retention logic.
impacts.rationale: REQ-004 to REQ-006 require persistent event records.

impacts.impact: Add a new event message using CAN ID 0x18FF50E5 and verify latency.
impacts.rationale: REQ-007 adds a new interface behavior.

impacts.impact: Provide a method to configure pre-warning and display sensor fault.
impacts.rationale: Configuration and sensor-fault indication need a user-facing mechanism, but the exact HMI is not stated.

impacts.impact: Confirm current non-volatile storage endurance/capacity and CPU/RAM margin are sufficient for 10,000 records and added logic.
impacts.rationale: The source says internal NVM exists but does not prove capacity/endurance/resource margin.

impacts.impact: Extend tests for thresholds, hysteresis, overload de-duplication, NVM, CAN timing, invalid sensors, and legacy behavior.
impacts.rationale: REQ-001 through REQ-010 introduce new behaviors and regression obligations.

risks.risk: A continuous overload could generate many duplicate event records.
risks.cause: The source says log every event but does not define event start/end or de-duplication.
risks.impact: Storage may fill rapidly and event history may be misleading.
risks.mitigation: Define a distinct overload event state model and acceptance tests before implementation.

risks.risk: CAN integration may be implemented incompatibly with the receiving node.
risks.cause: Payload mapping, scaling, byte order, and retry behavior are missing.
risks.impact: The message may be timely but unusable or misinterpreted.
risks.mitigation: Obtain an agreed interface-control definition and test with the receiver or bus simulation.

risks.risk: Fail-safe behavior may trigger too early, too late, or recover incorrectly.
risks.cause: Invalidity definition and exact 200 ms boundary/recovery semantics are unspecified.
risks.impact: Unexpected lift inhibition or insufficient fault response.
risks.mitigation: Define signal-validity criteria, timer semantics, and recovery/latching requirements; verify with fault injection.

risks.risk: NVM may not meet record capacity or endurance needs.
risks.cause: Record size, write frequency, memory allocation, and endurance margin are not provided.
risks.impact: Data loss, premature wear, or inability to meet 10,000-record retention.
risks.mitigation: Create a memory/endurance budget and implement integrity strategy suitable for the existing hardware.

risks.risk: Existing 90% warning or 100% inhibit behavior could regress when new threshold logic is introduced.
risks.cause: Warning state logic is being modified close to existing critical behavior.
risks.impact: Previously approved functionality could change unintentionally.
risks.mitigation: Maintain explicit state separation and execute baseline regression tests around threshold boundaries.

test_cases.title: Configure pre-warning threshold across valid and invalid range
test_cases.preconditions: Controller is operational and configuration mechanism is available.
steps: Verify default threshold after applicable default-initialization condition.
Set threshold to 80% and verify acceptance.
Set threshold to 90% and verify acceptance.
Attempt values below 80% and above 90%.
Restart or power-cycle if persistence is intended once that requirement is clarified.
test_cases.expected_result: Default is 85%; 80–90% values are supported; out-of-range values cannot result in an active configuration.

test_cases.title: Verify pre-warning activation and hysteresis release
steps: Increase calculated load from below T to T.
Verify pre-warning activation according to the agreed boundary.
Reduce load to just above T-5 percentage points.
Verify warning remains active.
Reduce load to the agreed release boundary at or below T-5.
test_cases.expected_result: Warning activates at the defined threshold and does not chatter; it clears only at the agreed hysteresis release boundary.

test_cases.title: Create and validate one overload event record
test_cases.preconditions: Event storage has free capacity and timestamp source is configured.
steps: Drive calculated load from below 100% SWL to 100% or above.
Read the resulting event record.
Compare stored load, boom angle, radius, and timestamp against the event inputs.
test_cases.expected_result: One correctly associated event record is stored with all required fields, subject to final event-definition semantics.

test_cases.title: Verify overload event de-duplication and full-storage behavior
test_cases.preconditions: Event definition and full-storage policy have been clarified.
steps: Hold load continuously above 100% SWL for a defined interval.
Observe number of stored events.
Populate storage to at least 10,000 records.
Trigger another event at the capacity boundary.
test_cases.expected_result: Logging follows the agreed event-definition and capacity policy without unintended record storms or silent corruption.

test_cases.title: Verify CAN overload-event identifier, content, and latency
test_cases.preconditions: CAN payload specification is available and bus monitoring is connected.
steps: Generate a known overload event.
Capture the event-detection timestamp.
Capture CAN traffic.
Verify identifier 0x18FF50E5.
Verify payload against the approved mapping.
Measure event-to-transmission latency.
test_cases.expected_result: The latest event is represented by the specified CAN message and transmission begins/completes within the agreed interpretation of the 500 ms requirement.

test_cases.title: Inject invalid load input around 200 ms boundary
test_cases.preconditions: A test method exists to force load-input validity state.
steps: Force load input invalid for less than the agreed 200 ms boundary and restore it.
Observe fault indication and inhibit relay.
Force load input invalid continuously beyond the agreed boundary.
Observe fault indication and inhibit relay.
Restore validity and observe recovery behavior once specified.
test_cases.expected_result: Responses match the agreed timing boundary; beyond-threshold invalidity produces both sensor-fault indication and lift-inhibit activation.

test_cases.title: Inject invalid boom-angle input around 200 ms boundary
test_cases.preconditions: A test method exists to force boom-angle validity state.
steps: Repeat the invalidity-duration boundary sequence for boom-angle input.
Verify sensor-fault indication.
Verify lift-inhibit relay activation beyond the specified duration.
test_cases.expected_result: Boom-angle invalidity invokes the same required fail-safe outputs at the agreed timing boundary.

test_cases.title: Regression test existing warning and lift-inhibit functions
test_cases.preconditions: Approved baseline behavior/test evidence is available.
steps: Execute baseline warning tests not superseded by ECN-042.
Execute baseline 100% SWL lift-inhibit tests.
Confirm sensor and relay hardware remain unchanged.
Compare results with approved baseline expectations.
test_cases.expected_result: Unaffected baseline warning/inhibit behavior remains unchanged and excluded hardware is not modified.

action_items.action: Define overload-event start/end and duplicate suppression semantics.
Provide CAN payload mapping, scaling, byte order, and retry expectations for ID 0x18FF50E5.
Define timestamp source, resolution, rollover, and behavior when time is invalid.
Define storage-full policy and confirm memory/endurance budget.
Define invalid-sensor detection criteria and recovery/latching behavior.
Identify approved baseline regression tests for existing warning/inhibit behavior.

clarification_questions: What user/interface mechanism configures the pre-warning threshold, what is the step size, and must the value persist across power cycles?
At exactly threshold minus 5 percentage points, should the pre-warning clear or remain active?
What defines one overload event: threshold crossing, a continuous above-100% episode, or every sampling instant?
When 10,000 records are stored, should the controller stop logging, overwrite oldest records, raise a diagnostic, or use another policy?
What is the CAN payload byte mapping, scaling, byte order, DLC, transmission/retry policy, and receiver expectation?
What timestamp source and resolution are required, and what should happen if valid time is unavailable?
What conditions make load or boom-angle input 'invalid', and should the fault/lift inhibit latch or auto-recover?
What approved baseline specification/test set defines the existing warning and inhibit behavior that must not regress?
confidence_notes: The source is sufficient to identify major functional changes but not sufficient for final implementation approval.
Several impacts are explicitly marked Inferred because the ECN specifies behavior but not architecture.
No external safety standard or compliance claim has been added because none was provided in the source.
